name: decision_tree
description: A left-to-right decision tree with health-economics conventions: decision nodes are squares, chance nodes are circles, terminal nodes are triangles. Branches carry labels, probabilities, and terminals carry payoffs (e.g. QALYs) and costs. Choose this scene for decision analysis, treatment comparisons, expected-value examples, cost-effectiveness of options, or any 'decision tree' request. Node positions are computed by a tidy-tree algorithm — never place nodes yourself. With `rollback: true` the template computes the tree itself — never do the arithmetic by hand: each chance node's expected payoff (and expected cost) is Σ p × child, written under it as value_<id>; each decision takes its best option (highest expected payoff, or with `wtp` the highest payoff × wtp − cost), marked best_<decision>_<option>, the others cut with prune_<decision>_<option>; a chance branch left without a probability gets 1 − the others. When terminals have costs the root decision's options also appear in a strategy table under the tree (cost, effect, incremental cost and effect, ICER, dominated / ext. dominated). Every computed number is live in drawn text as {tree.<key>} (ev_<id>, cost_<id>, icer_<optionId>). A big tree: set `collapsed: true` on a subtree to draw it as one node with its value.

root.description: The root node (usually a decision). Recursive structure.

id.description: Short id used in element ids (e.g. "surgery" → node_surgery). Give every node one so your commands can reference them.

value.description: Chance/decision node only: its folded-back value, e.g. "EV 11.6 y". Shown under the node as value_<id>; draw it on the beat that computes it. With rollback the value is computed — set this only to override its text.

collapsed.description: Chance/decision node only: draw the node without its subtree (a fan of stubs, collapsed_<id>); under rollback its value is still computed from the hidden subtree. For showing a big tree in parts.

probability.description: Chance-node branches only (0–1), summing to 1 across siblings. With rollback one sibling may omit it: it gets 1 − the others.

cost.description: Optional cost paid on this branch (e.g. the procedure itself); under rollback added to everything after it.

node.description: The child node (same structure as root).

rollback.description: Compute the tree: expected values under every chance/decision node, each decision's best branch marked, missing probabilities filled in, and (with costs) the strategy table. Default false: only what you write is drawn.

wtp.description: Willingness to pay per unit of payoff (e.g. 30000 per QALY). With costs, decisions then maximise payoff × wtp − cost; without it they maximise expected payoff.

unit.description: The payoff's unit, e.g. "QALYs": names the table's effect column.

table.description: false hides the strategy table (default: shown under rollback when terminals have costs and the root is a decision).

element_ids.edge_<parentId>_<childId>: the branch line between two nodes
element_ids.value_<id>: a chance/decision node's value text: its `value` param, or under rollback the computed expected payoff (and cost), e.g. value_surgery
element_ids.best_<decisionId>_<childId>: rollback: the highlighter under the branch a decision takes (the group `best` names all of them)
element_ids.prune_<decisionId>_<childId>: rollback: the // mark across each branch a decision rejects (the group `pruned` names all of them)
element_ids.collapsed_<id>: the stubs on a node with collapsed: true
element_ids.strategy_table: rollback with costs: the whole table under the tree (a group of strategy_head, strategy_rule and the rows)
element_ids.strategy_row_<childId>: one table row per option of the root decision, sorted by cost, e.g. strategy_row_surgery

examples.request: Draw a decision tree comparing surgery vs. medication with probabilities and QALY payoffs.
Cost-effectiveness of surgery, medication or watchful waiting as a decision tree: fold it back and show the ICERs at $50,000 per QALY.
Show only the top of a big screening tree; fold back the hidden part.
